No. The 2022 loss was not detected with Sentinel-2. It was mapped by Hansen/UMD Global Forest Change (GFC-2025-v1.13), which uses 30 m pixels and annual data. It shows about 0.6 ha of tree-cover loss in 2022, or 3.41% of the 17.6 ha asset.

Sentinel-2 does not appear among the sources used. The JRC GFC2020 reference map is 10 m, but it is a forest/non-forest map for 2020, not a loss detection. It agrees with the event area on 100% of it. The MGAP 2021 map puts 0.5 ha of the loss in native forest and 0.1 ha outside mapped forest.

Another 0.2 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was seen in 2022 but not counted as an event.

This evidence doesn't show whether deforestation occurred, what caused the loss, whether it was legal, who was responsible, or any compliance status.
